title: EV Charging Station App
description: An EV charging station mobile app that helps electric vehicle drivers find nearby chargers, check real-time availability, book a slot, and pay for charging from one simple app.

details.subtitle: A driver-first EV charging app that makes finding, booking, and paying for a charger effortless
details.text: EV Charging Station App is a mobile app for electric vehicle owners who need charging to be as simple as filling up with fuel. For many EV drivers, range anxiety starts with not knowing where the next working charger is, whether it fits their car, or whether someone else is already using it. We led the complete UI/UX design of the app. This covered the map-based station finder, station details with live charger availability, connector and power filters, slot booking, the live charging session screen, in-app payments and wallet, and charging history. The design keeps key information such as distance, price per kWh, charger speed and battery progress visible at a glance, so drivers can make quick decisions on the road with confidence.
problem: EV drivers struggled to find nearby charging stations they could rely on, and often arrived to find chargers busy, out of order, or incompatible with their vehicle.
Important details such as connector type, charging speed, price per kWh and live availability were scattered or missing, which made it hard to compare stations quickly.
Charging sessions felt like a black box: drivers could not easily see battery progress, time remaining, or the cost building up while they waited.
Payments were fragmented across different operators, cards and apps, which added friction at the charger and made spending hard to track.
solution: Designed a map-first station finder with clear availability pins, distance, and price, so drivers can spot the nearest free and compatible charger in seconds.

Built smart filters for connector type (CCS, Type 2, CHAdeMO), charging speed (AC or DC fast charging), price, and amenities, plus detailed station pages with photos, ratings, and live charger status.
Introduced slot booking and turn-by-turn navigation handoff, so drivers can reserve a charger before they arrive and avoid waiting in a queue.
Created a live charging session screen with a battery progress ring, kWh delivered, estimated time to full, and running cost, with notifications when charging is complete.
Simplified payments with a built-in wallet, saved cards, and itemized receipts, along with a charging history view that tracks energy used, money spent, and CO₂ saved over time.

title: ClauseLedger
description: An AI-powered contract analysis dashboard that turns lengthy signed contracts into structured, trustworthy financial data, so finance teams can see what they are owed, what they owe, and what needs attention at a glance.

details.subtitle: Every signed promise, accounted for: an AI contract intelligence dashboard for finance teams
details.text: ClauseLedger is a B2B web app that helps finance and revenue teams get the numbers out of signed customer contracts that often run to 150-200 pages. Finance analysts usually read every agreement by hand and retype billing terms, due dates and commitments into spreadsheets and CRM systems, which is slow and error-prone. We designed a tool that extracts, structures and verifies that information automatically. The work followed a full UX process. We started with problem framing and research notes, then built a user persona around Sarah, a finance analyst at a mid-size B2B SaaS company. From there we sketched the information architecture and user flows on paper, turned them into a digital IA in Figma, and finished with high-fidelity visual design for the login, dashboard, contracts portfolio, task and reporting screens. The result is a calm, data-dense interface. At a glance it shows money owed, money owed out, revenue at risk, and which contract clauses still need a human review.
problem: Key financial terms were buried across 150-200 page contracts, so finding billing conditions, commitments and deadlines took finance teams hours of manual reading.
Analysts had to copy contract details into spreadsheets and CRM systems by hand, which led to repeated effort, inconsistent data and missed revenue.
Billing triggers, renewal notices, opt-out windows and payment terms were easy to overlook. Missed invoices and costly contractual deadlines followed.
Teams lacked confidence in manually extracted data and kept going back to the original contract to check it, which slowed down the whole workflow.
Even when the information was available, it was hard to tell what action was needed, who owned it and when it was due, especially across a large portfolio of contracts.
solution: Designed a simple upload-and-extract flow where a contract is ingested and AI turns its key terms, billing information, due dates and commitments into structured data that is easy to scan.

Built a finance-first dashboard with four headline KPI cards: Owed to Us, We Owe, Revenue at Risk and Awaiting Review. Each card is paired with a prioritized "Needs Attention" queue, so critical issues such as unbilled milestones or CRM mismatches come up first with a clear Review, Decide or Compare action.

Brought upcoming billing, upcoming deadlines and a Portfolio Health breakdown (Verified, Needs Review, Exceptions, Processing, Archived) into a single view, so renewals, notice periods and invoice triggers are never missed.

Created a contracts portfolio table with contract value, next key date, CRM match status, an AI confidence meter, status chips and owner avatars, so analysts can instantly spot low-confidence extractions and discrepancies.
Made every extracted value traceable back to its source clause, with confidence thresholds and verification states, which cuts down re-checking and gives teams confidence in the data they report.

Grounded the whole experience in a researched user persona, hand-sketched information architecture and user flows, and a structured navigation of Dashboard, Contracts, My Tasks, Reports and Settings, so the product reflects how finance analysts actually work.

title: Habit Tracking App
description: A gamified habit tracking mobile app that helps people build daily routines, keep streaks alive, and grow virtual plants as a reward for consistency.

details.subtitle: A gamified habit tracker that turns daily routines into a rewarding self-care journey
details.text: Habit Tracking is a mobile app designed to help people build and maintain daily routines such as reading, sleeping on time, exercising, and meditating. Instead of treating habit-building as a plain checklist, the app layers in streak flames, achievement badges, and a "grow your plants" reward system, turning consistency into something genuinely satisfying to watch grow. We led the complete UI/UX design of the app, from the daily task screen and weekly/monthly/yearly progress views to the add-habit flow, individual habit analytics, activity heatmaps, and the achievements screen.
problem: Most habit trackers feel like sterile checklists, so users lose motivation and abandon the app within the first few days.
Users needed a single home screen that could switch between Today, Weekly, Monthly, and Yearly views without losing context or requiring deep navigation.
Long-term consistency data such as streaks, completion rate, and historical activity needed to feel rewarding to look at, not just accurate.
solution: Designed color-coded habit cards, each with its own icon, color, and live streak counter, so the daily list is instantly scannable and every check-in feels like a small visual win.

Built a unified Today / Weekly / Monthly / Yearly switcher anchored by a circular progress ring and a per-day streak grid, letting users zoom into today's tasks or zoom out across weeks in a single tap.

Introduced a "grow your plants" gamification layer with streak flames, milestone badges (10, 50, 100, 300 completions), perfect-day achievements, and an activity heatmap, turning habit tracking into an ongoing, game-like progress journey.
Simplified habit creation into one clean bottom-sheet flow covering name, description, tracking type (task, amount, or time), color, and frequency, so setting up a new habit takes seconds.

details.text: Uniite is a matchmaking platform built around a simple belief: the wisdom and involvement of parents shouldn't be lost just because matchmaking has gone digital. We designed and developed uniite.co end-to-end, crafting an experience where parents and their children can shortlist, discuss, and connect with potential matches together, backed by a visual identity that feels warm, trustworthy, and refined rather than transactional or app-like.

Most matrimonial sites rely on dated, form-heavy UI patterns that feel closer to classifieds than a curated, premium matchmaking experience.
Parents and children needed a shared space to participate in the matchmaking journey together, without either generation feeling sidelined or excluded from key decisions.
solution: Designed a warm, editorial visual identity built on a deep maroon (#6B0606) and soft ivory (#FDF3EC) palette, paired with the elegant serif pairing of Albra Trial for headlines and Canela for body copy, to evoke heritage, trust, and premium curation.

Created dual-perspective browsing and shortlisting flows that let parents and their children collaborate on matches together, keeping the process transparent while respecting each generation's comfort level.
Simplified onboarding and profile-building into a guided, story-like flow instead of a long static form, reducing drop-off and making the platform feel personal rather than bureaucratic.

Established a clear content hierarchy with deep charcoal headings (#181514) over softer supporting copy (#6A6A6A), so every profile stays easy to scan and comfortable to read on a warm, low-glare background.
